 Apple confirms iCloud outage as users report issues with Apple Pay, App Store and other services
 Following a string of high-profile online service outages this past week, several Apple services appear to be experiencing issues today.
 Dan Thorp-Lancaster Follow Editor Updated Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Updated Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC If you're having trouble signing into iCloud or other Apple services today, you aren't alone. (NurPhoto via Getty Images) Apple appears to be experiencing issues with its online services today, preventing some users from signing into iCloud and other Apple services. According to Downdetector , a site that tracks reports of online service outages, iCloud, Apple Support, Apple Pay, and the App Store are all seeing spikes in reports. Apple's support page currently shows it's having issues with iCloud accounts and sign-ins, along with other services.
 According to Downdetector reports, these are the services that saw spikes in outage reports:
 Apple Support
 iCloud,
 Apple Pay
 App Store
 Apple Business Manager
 Apple Music
 Apple Store
 Sign In With Apple
 Apple Card
 Advertisement Advertisement In addition to iCloud, Apple's support page also flags that AppleCare on Device, which lets you purchase AppleCare on your phone or tablet, is experiencing an outage. As of 1:10 p.m. ET, the page also listed the App Store and Apple Music as experiencing an outage. Around 1:41 p.m. ET, the affected services on Downdetector started showing a slight downward trend in reports.
 Users online reported being signed out of services and unable to sign back in. Others reported being unable to activate new iPhones.
 Apple didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
 The issues follow a string of outages that have plagued online services over the past week. On Nov. 12, Microsoft Outlook and Teams were knocked out for more than 30 hours due to what Microsoft described as a technical issue. On Nov. 13, a technical issue caused all air traffic across the U.S. to be grounded , leading to thousands of canceled and delayed flights.
 Advertisement Advertisement On Monday, online services at several major U.S. banks experienced problems for several hours after an issue with JPMorgan Chase's systems. Today, CNN reported that a highly classified communications network used by the National Security Agency (NSA) went down.
